clue.text: She can't grasp novel I mused about

indicators.note: turned about, the words that follow are scrambled out of their order

blocks.note: all eleven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman who cannot get her head round a novel the speaker was musing over.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venus de Milo is the famous armless Greek statue in the Louvre, so she literally cannot grasp anything.
explanation.definitionFit: The statue lost both arms long ago, so it has no hands with which to hold any object.

clue.text: Compile ten diverse tests for those claiming special needs

indicators.note: to compile is to put together anew, so the following letters are assembled in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An instruction to put together assorted exams for pupils who say they need extra support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diverse' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'Compile' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups with a personal stake in an outcome push for treatment that favours their own particular demands.

clue.text: Female spirit essential to sonata Grieg made

indicators.note: the essential part of something is its core, so only the central letters of each following word count

blocks.note: the two central letters of a six-letter word
the central letter of a five-letter word
the two central letters of a four-letter word

explanation.surface: A water sprite is the heart of a sonata Grieg composed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a naiad is a nymph living in a spring, river or lake.

clue.text: Spanish agreement to adopt multi-variable incentives

indicators.note: something variable can change its form, so the word before it is rearranged
adopting means taking in, so one piece is placed inside the other

explanation.surface: A Spanish deal accepts a complex multi-variable approach to motivation.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'multi-variable' hides the join between fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimuli are things that rouse action or response, which is what incentives provide.

clue.text: Extra! Extra! Leaders concealing crops loss

indicators.note: leaders are the ones in front, so only the opening letter of each exclamation is used
to conceal is to hide inside, so the pair of leaders wrap around the next piece

blocks.note: first letter of each of the two words
to crop is to clip, and both work as plural nouns too

explanation.surface: A newspaper seller's cry announcing a headline about a failed harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra! Extra!' is the newsboy's call, but here it only supplies two initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclipse is a loss of light, and figuratively a loss of standing or importance.

clue.text: Breathing excitedly with run out secured

indicators.note: excited breathing is irregular, so the letters of that word are jumbled
put out means removed, so that abbreviation is struck from the word

blocks.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Panting after a cricket run-out that has sealed the match.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R from BREATHING, leaving BEATHING, then rearrange those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an outcome already certain, as good as won and safely locked away.

clue.text: Invite trouble when preparing early bird meal?

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for stirring up a mass of problems
second meaning, literal and comic: getting a tin ready for the bird who rises first

explanation.walkthrough: The early bird catches the worm, so its meal would be tinned worms; 'early bird meal' also suggests a cheap restaurant deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means starting something that unleashes many complications, and literally means unsealing a tin of grubs.

clue.text: Castaway picked up broadcast by sailors

indicators.note: picked up as on a radio receiver, meaning the words are heard rather than read

blocks.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it

explanation.surface: A shipwrecked man rescued after his message was heard on a sailors' radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests radio, but means scattering seed. Robinson Crusoe is Defoe's shipwrecked hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's hero spent years alone on an island after his ship was wrecked, the archetypal marooned figure.

clue.text: Legend next to Bond?

blocks.note: a promise, as in 'my word is my bond'

explanation.surface: Is a legendary figure found alongside James Bond?
explanation.walkthrough: Bond looks like the spy, but it is a pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A byword is a person or thing so famous as an example that its name becomes proverbial.

clue.text: Italian scorer's second offence in Ireland

indicators.note: the preceding pieces sit within the abbreviation for the country

explanation.surface: An Italian footballer commits a second foul in a match in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' suggests a goal-getter but means one who writes musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini composed operas such as The Barber of Seville, so he was an Italian writer of musical scores.

clue.text: Chance of finding furry creature in outskirts of Laxey

indicators.note: the outskirts are the edges of a place, so only the first and last letters are taken
the animal sits within the edge letters of the place name

explanation.surface: What are the odds of spotting an otter on the edge of Laxey, a village on the Isle of Man?
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is a matter of pure luck, so anything left to chance can be called one.

clue.text: Career knock will slow your progress down

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun

blocks.note: to career is to rush along at speed

explanation.surface: A setback in someone's working life will hold back their advancement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' reads as a job, but here it is the verb meaning to hurtle.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised ridge across a road forces drivers to brake, slowing vehicles as they pass.

clue.text: She inspires weary author occasionally

indicators.note: only now and then, so every other letter of the following words is used

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A tired writer only sometimes finds a source of inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry, a goddess who gave poets ideas.

clue.text: Only half of them wait for discharge

indicators.note: keeping just half means the other half of each word is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written; its back half is kept
taken as written; its back half is kept

explanation.surface: Just half of a group are waiting to be released.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the last two letters of each four-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or give off, which is a verb sense of discharge.

clue.text: Energy firm recruits city guide — it could spark something off

indicators.note: a company recruiting takes people in, so the guide goes inside the word for firm

blocks.note: an A-Z is a street atlas, famously of London

explanation.surface: A power company takes on a tour guide for the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy firm' reads as one business, but the words split into two adjectives' worth of letters. The A-Z is the classic British street map book.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything likely to ignite and start a blaze is a danger, literally able to cause a fire.

clue.text: It gives potter one after table ends secured

indicators.note: the ends are the extremities, so only the first and last letters of the furniture word are taken
coming after means placed second, so the snooker phrase follows the edge letters of the furniture

blocks.note: in snooker, potting a red ball scores one point

explanation.surface: A ceramicist is given something once the table edges are fixed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like a maker of pots but is a snooker player who pots balls; each red is worth one point.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal or boat that is tethered is tied fast with a rope, so it is held secure.

clue.text: Calculate moth deaths resulting from mutation

indicators.note: a mutation is a change of form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A biologist works out how many moths have died because of a genetic mutation.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal British idiom means to work out the figures, to do the arithmetic.

clue.text: Fools buttonholed doctor in pairs

indicators.note: to buttonhole someone is to hold them in conversation, so one piece is held within another

explanation.surface: Idiots cornered a physician, working two at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbo is an informal insult for a stupid person, so the plural means silly people.

clue.text: Rawness surprisingly can give you what you're looking for here

indicators.note: a surprising arrangement is an unexpected one, so the letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Being raw and unpolished might unexpectedly help you find what you seek.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the crossword itself: what solvers seek in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone doing a puzzle is hunting for solutions, the words that fit each clue.

clue.text: That woman's taking in newspaper that is more powerful

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing, so the following pieces go inside the pronoun

blocks.note: id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A woman reading a paper that has extra clout.
explanation.definitionFit: Hefty means big and strong, so the comparative describes something with greater force.

clue.text: Entertainer gets laugh changing square to circle  …

indicators.note: one shape is swapped for the other, so one letter in the laugh is exchanged

blocks.note: S as the abbreviation for square
a circle is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A comedian gets a laugh by turning a square into a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: One O of HOOT becomes S; the clue's wording reads the swap the other way round, between the circle and the square.
explanation.definitionFit: A host entertains guests at a party, or presents a show on television.

clue.text: Outburst, as I get stuck in traffic

indicators.note: to be stuck in something is to be trapped inside it

blocks.note: to traffic is to trade, illicitly or not

explanation.surface: Someone explodes with rage while stuck in a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traffic' paints a road jam but means commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, an eruption of furious words.

clue.text: …  it starts mostly in response to humour

definitions.text: it starts mostly in response to humour

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the first letter of each is used

blocks.note: initial letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Following on from the comedian, laughter mostly begins in reaction to jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses tie this to the clue before it: the host's laugh continues here.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirth is merriment and laughter, the response that comic jokes are meant to provoke.

clue.text: We stop for broadcast that's quietly influential

definitions.note: an adjective phrase standing for the noun

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio presenter pauses for a programme with subtle sway.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft power is a nation's ability to persuade through culture and diplomacy rather than force.

clue.text: Punishment after removing an extremely small amount of money

definitions.note: the plural names a tiny sum

indicators.note: removing means taking away, so the following little word is cut out

blocks.note: an act of self-punishment for sin

explanation.surface: A fine reduced to a tiny sum.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove AN from the middle of PENANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pence are the smallest British coins, so a few of them is a trifling sum.

clue.text: Note stink over ball delivery

indicators.note: turned over, the preceding word is read from the end backwards

blocks.note: the stroke that puts the ball in play in tennis

explanation.surface: A smell is noticed as the ball is bowled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' suggests cricket, which fits 'ball delivery', but it reverses BO.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to notice or remark on it, which is what observing means.

clue.text: Overlooked bidder on giving piece back

indicators.note: a piece is a part, so the letters come from within the run of words
going back means reading right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the third

explanation.surface: An auction bidder is passed over after offering a part back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overlooked has been disregarded or not noticed, the sense of being ignored.

clue.text: Not the main way nurses get assigned to teams, reportedly

indicators.note: reported means told by voice, so the words are heard rather than spelt

explanation.surface: Hospital nurses are reportedly allocated to different groups.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, the two words run into each other: the S of the first slides onto the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Side streets are minor roads branching off the main thoroughfare.
